name: Fisher Covered Railroad Bridge
facts: The Fisher Covered Railroad Bridge, built in 1908 by Boston and Maine Railroad, was the last covered bridge in the United States to carry railroad traffic when listed on the National Register in 1974.

Its double Town lattice truss design stretches 103.5 feet, a rare surviving example of this engineering style in Vermont, and its gabled roof features a distinctive central monitor that lights the interior.
In 1968, facing demolition for a steel truss, a pier and four steel girders were added to support the historic bridge, preserving its timber trusses while modernizing its load capacity.
